fichas.title: Emergency Generator Rooms
fichas.summary: Diesel generator sets provide emergency power during outages. The room layout, ventilation, exhaust, sound insulation, and openings depend on generator capacity and configuration. Diagrams show separate air supply and extraction, and an exhaust route to above the roof. Spring dampers can reduce sound transmission into the structure.
uses: Provide emergency electricity during power cuts
Supply emergency and safety lighting, lifts, and other critical loads

dimensions.context: stated performance range for diesel generator sets
dimensions.ocr_raw: The performance range is between 5 and 2000 kVA

EMERGENCY POWER ROOMS

Emergency power supply systems (diesel generator sets)
Emergency power units are combustion motors (usually diesel)
which are coupled to generators to produce electricity. They are
used for a limited time in case of a power cut (and are thus not for
constant power supply) and supply emergency and safety lighting,
lifts and other critical usages (e.g. in operating theatres in hospitals, server rooms and industrial processes etc.). They consist of a
diesel motor and a generator mounted on a base frame (e.g. steel)
on a foundation with elastic supports between machine set and
frame, and a starter and battery ---7 0.

Fuel tank

0

There are mobile (container generator sets) and permanently installed diesel generator sets including switching gear. The performance range is between 5 and 2000 kVA (kilovolt amp) according
to specification.

Exhaust pipe
to above roof

The design starts with the determination of:
- motor power
- sound insulation
- exhaust system

On account of the high noise level involved in running a generator
set for testing and maintenance, it is recommended not to place
it near inhabited rooms which should be particularly quiet (e.g.
the care rooms of a hospital). Measures should also be undertaken to keep the noise level as low as possible. Another measure
is to position the frame, on which the generator and motor are
mounted, on spring dampers to reduce the sound transmission
into the structure.

Uninterruptible power supply {UPS) systems
There is normally a gap of at most 15 seconds between the power
cut and the switching to emergency power. UPS systems are used
to continue power supply without interruption during this time.
Static UPS systems are bridging battery power devices, whose
batteries are constantly charged from the mains.

Extract

Battery
Room for diesel emergency power generator with separate air supply and
extraction

Extract

Emergency power rooms
The required dimensions, height and openings of the room for a
generator set vary according to the power and configuration of
the motor ---7 f). Air supply and extraction can be through forced
ventilation (shaft) ---7 0. It is also possible to run the extract air
together with the exhaust of the diesel motor up a vertical shaft
to exit above the roof ---7 f) - 0. In this case, sufficient sound
insulation should be provided with a silencer in the ductwork ---7
f) - 0. The manufacturers of the motors give information about
the required quantity of air and thus the size of the supply and
extract ducts.

It

According to equipment and requirements, a UPS system should
be able to protect the connected consumer from the following
risks: power cuts, voltage fluctuations, voltage peaks, low voltage,
excessive voltage, lightning effects/switching peaks, interference
voltage and frequency fluctuations.
While UPS systems are designed to cope with a power cut of at
most 30-60 minutes, diesel-powered emergency generators can
supply power during much longer interruptions.

Emergency power supply systems (diesel generator sets)
Emergency power units are combustion motors (usually diesel)
which are coupled to generators to produce electricity. They are
used for a limited time in case of a power cut (and are thus not for
constant power supply) and supply emergency and safety lighting,
lifts and other critical usages (e.g. in operating theatres in hospitals, server rooms and industrial processes etc.). They consist of a
diesel motor and a generator mounted on a base frame (e.g. steel)
on a foundation with elastic supports between machine set and
frame, and a starter and battery ---7 0.

Fuel tank

0

There are mobile (container generator sets) and permanently installed diesel generator sets including switching gear. The performance range is between 5 and 2000 kVA (kilovolt amp) according
to specification.

Exhaust pipe
to above roof

The design starts with the determination of:
- motor power
- sound insulation
- exhaust system

set for testing and maintenance, it is recommended not to place
it near inhabited rooms which should be particularly quiet (e.g.

Uninterruptible power supply {UPS) systems
There is normally a gap of at most 15 seconds between the power
cut and the switching to emergency power. UPS systems are used
to continue power supply without interruption during this time.
Static UPS systems are bridging battery power devices, whose
batteries are constantly charged from the mains.

Emergency power rooms
The required dimensions, height and openings of the room for a
generator set vary according to the power and configuration of
the motor ---7 f). Air supply and extraction can be through forced
ventilation (shaft) ---7 0. It is also possible to run the extract air
together with the exhaust of the diesel motor up a vertical shaft
to exit above the roof ---7 f) - 0. In this case, sufficient sound
insulation should be provided with a silencer in the ductwork ---7
f) - 0. The manufacturers of the motors give information about
the required quantity of air and thus the size of the supply and
extract ducts.

It

According to equipment and requirements, a UPS system should
be able to protect the connected consumer from the following
risks: power cuts, voltage fluctuations, voltage peaks, low voltage,
excessive voltage, lightning effects/switching peaks, interference
voltage and frequency fluctuations.
While UPS systems are designed to cope with a power cut of at
most 30-60 minutes, diesel-powered emergency generators can
supply power during much longer interruptions.

fichas.title: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) Systems
fichas.summary: Static UPS systems use batteries that are continuously charged from the mains to bridge the interval between a power cut and emergency power switching. They protect connected equipment from outages and power-quality disturbances. UPS systems cover a short interruption; diesel generators can supply power for longer outages.
uses: Maintain uninterrupted power during transfer to emergency supply
Protect connected equipment from power cuts, voltage variations, lightning effects, and frequency fluctuations
